$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Virtual networks. See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.vnets.vnet.crud.title: Virtual networks (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.vnets.address_space.title: Address space (IPv4 prefixes)
limitations: Only IPv4 CIDR prefixes are modelled; IPv6 address spaces are not.

azure.vnets.subnets.title: Subnets (Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/subnets)
limitations: Name, address range, the private-subnet (defaultOutboundAccess) flag, NSG, route table and NAT gateway associations are real and drive behaviour (system routes incl. None for RFC1918 outside the vnet, UDRs, NAT/default outbound egress). The console's Add subnet dialog's NAT gateway and Route table pickers select from real Microsoft.Network/natGateways and routeTables (created over ARM/CLI; this lens has no dedicated console for either yet, same as NSGs' earlier state). NIC private IPs are allocated from the subnet (.0-.3 and the last address reserved). Subnet delegation is not modelled.

Offline, the rules are enforced on REAL packets (one Docker bridge per subnet + an nftables table per space, core/netsim/enforce.py) only when VYOMI_NETSIM_ENFORCE=1|auto and the instance runs on the Docker compute backend; with enforcement off (the default) or on LXD/Multipass runtimes they are evaluated, not enforced.

azure.vnets.peerings.title: Virtual network peerings (Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/virtualNetworkPeerings)
limitations: Adding a peering creates the real ARM peering object on both virtual networks (same as the portal's Add blade), with peeringState fixed at 'Connected' and peeringSyncLevel fixed at 'FullyInSync' — Vyomi has no asynchronous sync process to model, so 'Sync' is a no-op refresh.
Traffic only crosses a peering once BOTH virtual networks hold a Connected link (one-sided links carry nothing), and it is non-transitive.

azure.vnets.service_endpoints.title: Service endpoints (subnet properties.serviceEndpoints)
limitations: A service endpoint is stored as a {service, locations} entry on the subnet, same as real ARM. Service endpoint policies (restricting which resource instances are reachable) are not modelled.

azure.vnets.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this virtual network
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this virtual network); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.vnets.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.vnets.export_template.title: Export template
limitations: The ARM Template, Bicep and Terraform tabs are all generated client-side from this resource's live ARM state; linked/nested templates and deployment history are not modelled.

azure.vnets.iam.title: Access control (IAM)
limitations: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions), and Check access / My access run the real wildcard + scope-inheritance + notActions + explicit-deny decision — all ENFORCED scoped to this virtual network (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view); Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too). Deny assignments and Classic administrators remain an honest gap — Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management and the legacy Azure Service Management administrator list are not modelled.

azure.vnets.tools.title: Diagnose and solve problems (remaining tiles), Resource visualizer, Tasks, Support + Troubleshooting
limitations: Resource visualizer, Tasks and Support + Troubleshooting are not built, and Diagnose and solve problems' other diagnostic tiles remain an honest gap. Its IP flow verify, Next hop and Connection troubleshoot tiles ARE built — see azure.vnets.network_watcher.

azure.vnets.network_watcher.title: Diagnose and solve problems / Monitoring: IP flow verify, Next hop, Connection troubleshoot (Network Watcher)
limitations: IP flow verify, Next hop and Connection troubleshoot all answer from the shared netsim evaluator (core/netsim) — the same engine behind AWS Reachability Analyzer and GCP Connectivity Tests — scoped to a virtual machine's network interface in this virtual network's subnets. Vyomi auto-provisions the regional NetworkWatcher_<location> resource the first time any of the three tools runs in a location, same as the real portal's 'Enable Network Watcher' behaviour. Connection troubleshoot's hop-by-hop trace uses Vyomi's own component labels (route-table/nsg/peering/...), not real Network Watcher's hop-type enum, and offers TCP/UDP (this evaluator's protocols) rather than real Azure's TCP/ICMP. There is no standalone Network Watcher service console yet, only these diagnostic tools reached from the NSG and Virtual network blades.

azure.vnets.topology.title: Topology (subnets, their connected devices, and peered virtual networks)
limitations: The data is real — the same ARM reads the Subnets, Connected devices and Peerings panels use (subnet address ranges, NSG/route table/NAT gateway associations, attached network interfaces, peering state) — but it is rendered as a structured list rather than Azure's interactive canvas diagram.

azure.vnets.monitoring.title: Alerts, Metrics, Diagnostic settings, Logs
limitations: Azure Monitor alert rules/diagnostic settings/metrics for virtual networks are not modelled.

azure.vnets.network_appliances.title: Azure Bastion, DDoS protection, Azure Firewall, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Network Manager, Private endpoints
limitations: Each of these is a separate resource type (bastionHosts, ddosProtectionPlans, azureFirewalls, privateEndpoints, networkManagers) or a security service Vyomi does not model; the virtual network create wizard's Bastion/Firewall/DDoS checkboxes and the resource menu items are an honest gap, not provisioned.

azure.vnets.connected_devices.title: Connected devices
limitations: The list is a real ARM read (every Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces resource in the subscription whose ipConfigurations[].subnet.id points at one of this vnet's subnets), so a NIC attached via ARM/the CLI/another tool shows up here. Device Type is always reported as 'Network interface' — Vyomi has no DHCP lease / ARP table to discover non-NIC clients (VMs/devices that never registered a network interface resource).

azure.vnets.ip_address_management.title: IP address pools (Allocate using IP address pools) and advertised address prefixes (BGP)
limitations: Azure IPAM pool allocation and custom BGP route advertisement are advanced features Vyomi doesn't model.
